note:
Alfred William Stanfield (#3554) is made a resident of **Lincoln House, Lincoln Circus (#403)**, on A. Hagues's decision. He is bound by number and this adds the house alone: **no census row is created**, because he was not enumerated there. On census night 1911 he was at Pattishall House near Towcester, visiting Frank Hawthorn Burn, and his own house was returned with only his three servants in it, the cook Annie Elizabeth Tune signing the schedule for him.

**The reasoning, which is elimination rather than a document.** The directory prints him on Lincoln Circus in 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16, always without a house name or number, and his obituary gives only 'his residence, Lincoln Circus, The Park'. The circus holds three properties. In 1911 Gladstone House was occupied by the Radfords, The Cottage by the Palmers, and **Lincoln House was empty** - the only vacancy on the circus in the year his servants were returned at an unnamed house on it. He is also the only Lincoln Circus resident the 1910-11 directory prints without a house against his name.

**Nothing contradicts it.** He died on 25 September 1918, and Harry Laurence Birkin's household of eight is at Lincoln House on the 1921 return - after him, with no overlap. Annie Elizabeth Tune, who kept the house for him in 1911, is cook at 8 Western Terrace with the Bradleys by 1921, which is what one expects of a servant whose household has broken up on the death of its head.

**What this is not.** No schedule names Lincoln House as his address; the case rests on the directory, the obituary, and the circus having no other empty house that year. If the 1911 round for Lincoln Circus is ever read and puts his servants somewhere else, this resident link is the thing to undo. The three servants' 1911 census rows are still unfiled under 'Lincoln Circus (house not named)' and want reassigning to #403, which an import cannot do. Lincoln House itself is demolished and its position in the record is approximate. See [[stanfield-lincoln-circus-house]].
source: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16, Lincoln Circus; his obituary, 'Mr. A. W. Stanfield: death in Nottingham of well-known barrister'; and the 1911 occupancy of the three Lincoln Circus properties. Identification by A. Hagues.
